text: Start with the molecule the membrane is built from, which you met in the lipids lessons: the phospholipid. It has a head containing a phosphate group, which is polar and carries charge, and two fatty-acid tails, which are non-polar. Water molecules are polar too, so they're attracted to the head and form hydrogen bonds with it: the head is hydrophilic. The tails can't form those interactions with water, so they're hydrophobic. One molecule, two very different ends.
